date.basis: not dated by the entry; site pottery list does not date components

features.quote: These pits can be identified as remains of quarrying
features.subtype: rock-hewn quarry recesses ('pits'), 5-30 m across, c. 1-2 m deep

features.quote: recesses and pits for drainage of local surface water

date.basis: not dated; Meshel says part of the remains are recent

notes: f1/f2: the quarrymen's village is 'in the northern part of the saddle' (the saddle = the site area), so direction N from the site; no distance. The entry's central grid (1934/1668) is c. 220 m from the unit point. f3: direction is from the settlement, so relative_to other. f4: Zertal's quarry recesses are open hollows the entry itself calls 'pits'; coded as pit for completeness, spread over the whole saddle, so no position. f5 may describe the same recesses. f6: Meshel puts it 'south of the road' (relative_to other); not called a pool, no size, so pool_def unclear; may be the same as f2. Data block 'Cisterns: 4'. Fig. 329 shows 3 'C' symbols and 'Pool?'; its north arrow points to the lower right of the page. The unit point cannot be placed on the plan (no grid), so no plan positions. Moat/fosse (open quarry trench) and lime kiln not coded. No graves.
